# Kalislav Smirnov, DevOps Engineer and Aerospace Engineer

> DevOps engineer with 4.5 years of experience in Kubernetes, GitLab CI/CD, Ansible and Terraform, most recently for banks and government agencies, including fully air-gapped environments. Also integrates SAST, DAST and SCA scanning into pipelines, and builds autonomous AI agents, MCP servers and RAG systems on Claude. Aerospace engineer by degree (Bauman Moscow State Technical University, spacecraft design; SolidWorks, KOMPAS-3D, ANSYS, MATLAB, Simulink). Based in Tbilisi, Georgia (GMT+4). Open to offers now: remote work for a company in any country, or relocation to the US, the EU (Cyprus included) or another popular destination (needs a work permit such as the EU Blue Card); full-time as an employee, B2B or contract; can start right away.

Book a 20-minute intro call: https://cal.com/kalikys/intro

Contact: kalikys@outlook.com · Telegram @kalikys · https://www.linkedin.com/in/devops-kalislav-smirnov/ · https://github.com/kalikys

## Field notes

- [Trivy was compromised twice in 2026. How a shared GitLab CI template for 90+ teams should run security scanners](https://kalik8s.com/blog/trivy-compromised-gitlab-ci-shared-template/): Trivy compromised in 2026 shows why a shared GitLab CI template must pin scanners by digest, mirror images and DBs into Nexus, and verify signatures.
- [Proxmox Terraform with bpg: 5 LXC containers, 6 cloud-init VMs and the state drift I caused myself](https://kalik8s.com/blog/proxmox-terraform-bpg-lxc-cloud-init/): bpg/proxmox Terraform provider in a real homelab on Proxmox VE 9: least-privilege API token, LXC, cloud-init VMs, import blocks, targeted applies, CI.
- [Air-gapped Nexus: delivering GPG-signed packages into a bank's closed network](https://kalik8s.com/blog/air-gapped-nexus-gpg-signed-package-delivery/): How packages get into an air gapped Nexus repository: sign on the connected side, verify before upload, keep an audit trail. Pattern, Python gate, Nexus API.
